name: cli-agent-runner
description: Run scoped Grok, Claude, Codex, or custom CLI workers with caller-defined responsibility roles: one worker, runner-brokered local descendants, or parent-declared independent leaf jobs, sharing CLI Agent Runner's default-on Codex IAB Live Console. Trigger on CLI Agent Runner, local orchestrator, Live Console, Grok/Claude CLI, custom runner JSON, or .cli-agent-runner continuation; explicit silent/no-console requests are the only OFF path; excludes generic coding and ordinary official subagents.

interface.shortDescription: Run CLI workers, brokered local descendants, or parallel leaf jobs with an IAB Live Console.
interface.longDescription: CLI Agent Runner is an explicit process-runner workflow for scoped CLI workers. Every role is a caller-defined responsibility label; the runner preallocates and enforces no role roster. `run --runner <id>` launches exactly one parent-managed worker; `--delegation-mode local_orchestrator` gives that worker a runner-owned loopback broker for bounded internal descendants; `orchestrate --runner <id> --jobs-file <json>` concurrently launches parent-declared independent responsibility leaves from a version-1 jobs file. The parent first derives human responsibility owners and their dependency graph, then splits only workstreams with stable handoffs and non-overlapping writable scopes when that materially reduces elapsed time; tightly coupled work remains with one owner. A hierarchy permission ceiling controls descendants only and never substitutes for sibling-job dispatch. Brokered descendants use unique IDs and non-overlapping focus scopes inside inherited task lineage, runner profile, authority scope, supervision, and decremented depth, then return to their immediate local orchestrator for integration. Codex, Claude, Grok, and custom profiles use this same provider-neutral broker path. It bundles Codex, Claude, and Grok profiles, accepts additional or overridden profiles from runner JSON, and invokes every profile through one validated command-and-arguments path. It starts and opens one token-protected Codex IAB Live Console at skill selection before worker preparation, keeps it alive across user-confirmation pauses, restores or reopens it before resuming, streams emitted stdout/stderr or structured messages, and shares it across all jobs with per-job and parent-child run IDs. It enforces a machine-checkable repository scope. A successful run or orchestration records its minimal completed result and stops without a follow-up collection, finalization, reviewer, or validator chain. Direct runner commands also own a console by default; only explicit silent or no-console selection disables it. It does not replace generic coding or ordinary official-subagent routing.
